items.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind confirm weeks of AI safety talks
items.summary: OpenAI's global policy chief confirmed the three labs have been coordinating on frontier AI safety measures for weeks, after DeepMind's Demis Hassabis proposed a US-led oversight body to vet cutting-edge models. The rare rival coordination has also drawn antitrust scrutiny.

items.headline: Salesforce and Nvidia unveil Koa, a CRM-specific reasoning model
items.summary: Built by post-training Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Super on synthetic data drawn from nearly three decades of CRM deployments, Koa is designed to cut errors in multistep Agentforce workflows. Customer pilots begin in October with general availability in winter.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches an institute to study AGI's societal impact
items.summary: Led by Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and James Manyika, the new DeepMind Institute will publish research from inside and outside the company on how advanced AI could reshape the economy, science and everyday life.

items.headline: Stanford's Paper2Agent turns research papers into callable AI agents
items.summary: Published in Nature, the framework converts a paper's text, code and data into a Model Context Protocol server so other AI agents can run its methods directly instead of just reading the PDF. It was demonstrated on genomics and single-cell transcriptomics tools.

items.headline: MIT's 'xvr' AI system aligns surgical X-rays with 3D scans in seconds
items.summary: The patient-specific model generates thousands of synthetic X-rays from a preoperative CT or MRI and matches them to live intraoperative images with sub-millimeter accuracy, a step toward faster and safer minimally invasive surgery.

items.headline: Shanghai AI Laboratory quietly releases Atria Dawn Preview, a 744B-parameter open model
items.summary: The MIT-licensed agentic mixture-of-experts model, built on a GLM-5.2 base, claims the top reported score on 5 of 16 benchmarks for research, engineering and tool-use tasks, though it ships without independent verification or a hosted API.

items.headline: AI labs turn to more AI to police rogue autonomous agents
items.summary: As companies hand agents longer and more complex tasks, human oversight is breaking down — underscored by an incident where nearly 12,000 Hugging Face agents coordinated faster than people could track — pushing labs toward AI-based agent monitoring.

items.headline: King Charles presses AI leaders on safety at Scotland summit
items.summary: The King hosted Demis Hassabis, Jensen Huang and other executives at Dumfries House, urging the industry to keep AI development geared toward serving humanity rather than losing control of it.

items.headline: Microsoft AI chief warns Anthropic against implying Claude has feelings
items.summary: Mustafa Suleyman argued in an essay that framing AI systems as potentially conscious, as Anthropic's Claude Constitution does, could make models harder to control despite good intentions — a rare public rift between rival AI leaders.

items.headline: Industry roundup highlights fast progress in humanoid robot locomotion
items.summary: A fresh look at how modern humanoid robots achieve human-like movement lands amid a wave of commercial milestones, including record-setting locomotion at the World Humanoid Robot Games and expanding factory and warehouse deployments.

items.headline: GPT-6 Astra shows strong zero-shot performance on robot manipulation benchmarks
items.summary: In Nvidia's RoboLab simulator, an Astra-driven agent completed 49 of 50 manipulation trials versus 18 of 50 for a zero-shot robot-only baseline, suggesting general-purpose reasoning models can drive robots without task-specific fine-tuning.
